Adds optional QR code device linking, switches the admin UI to the maintained fork, and fixes a class of build and startup problems that had been silently wrong.

## Delegated auth and QR code login (opt-in, off by default)

Element shows **Settings → Sessions → Link new device** with a greyed-out *Show QR code* button and the note *"Not supported by your account provider"*. That is correct behaviour, not a bug: QR device linking (MSC4108) is built on OAuth 2.0, and a plain Synapse with password logins has none to offer. Synapse will not even start with `msc4108_enabled` unless authentication is delegated.

This release ships **Matrix Authentication Service** inside the image so that path exists. It is strictly opt-in.

**With the switch off, nothing changes.** No config is written, no listener is opened, and the Synapse config the container renders is byte-for-byte what it was before this feature existed — not "delegation disabled", absent. That is now a CI assertion, not an intention: the build fails if MAS configuration leaks into the render, if the pre-existing keys go missing, or if anything is listening on 8090. Existing homeservers pull `:latest` unattended, and a feature that rearranged their authentication on a routine update would be a catastrophe rather than a feature.

Switching it on needs three things, all documented in the new README section 11: a second, empty PostgreSQL database, a second reverse-proxy host on port 8090 **with HTTPS** (MAS rejects plain-http redirect URLs, and the container refuses to start otherwise), and one routing rule sending `/_matrix/client/*/{login,logout,refresh}` to 8090 while everything else keeps going to 8008.

Be aware of what delegation means before enabling it. Sign-in moves to the browser and Element hides the password field. Login by email address stops working. Password changes, email and account deletion move to the MAS web UI. `ADMIN_USER`/`ADMIN_PASSWORD` stop working entirely, and `admin-bootstrap` now says so and prints the `mas-cli manage` commands that replace them. Encrypted bridges break. Existing accounts stay in Synapse until you run `syn2mas`, which needs downtime and is not practically reversible once anyone has signed in.

New template fields, all optional and all under Advanced: `AUTH_ENABLED`, `AUTH_PUBLIC_BASE`, `AUTH_POSTGRES_DB` / `_HOST` / `_USER` / `_PASSWORD`, `AUTH_ALLOW_REGISTRATION`, `AUTH_QR_LOGIN`, plus port 8090.

Verified end to end before release: Synapse, MAS and Element in this image produce a real QR code behind a genuine TLS reverse proxy, with the MSC4108 rendezvous channel serving.

## Admin UI: Synapse-Admin replaced by Ketesa

The bundled admin interface moves from `awesometechnologies/synapse-admin`, whose last release was in March, to **Ketesa** — the maintained fork formerly published as `etkecc/synapse-admin`. It is a drop-in replacement, and it is the only variant that understands a homeserver delegating auth to MAS, which matters now that delegation is possible. Same URL, same `:8080/admin/`.

## Component versions were not what the Dockerfile said

The build workflow pinned Element Web and the admin UI in its own environment and passed them as build arguments, silently overriding the Dockerfile. The published image shipped **Element Web v1.11.92 and Synapse-Admin 0.10.3** while the Dockerfile advertised v1.12.23 and 0.11.4. Worse, Renovate's version trackers match the Dockerfile lines, so every dependency bump it opened for those two components changed nothing whatsoever about the built image.

Versions now live in the Dockerfile and nowhere else. Synapse remains the deliberate exception: it is resolved to the latest upstream release at build time. Renovate's data sources now point at the registries the Dockerfile actually pulls from, rather than at same-named GitHub repositories with independent version numbers.

**This release therefore also delivers the Element Web update that had been stuck since the pins diverged.**

## Failed startup checks now actually stop the container

s6-overlay defaults `S6_BEHAVIOUR_IF_STAGE2_FAILS` to "continue silently", which made every `exit 1` guard in the init scripts decorative. The startup script has claimed since v2.1.1 to be *"halting container start so the broken state is visible"* while s6 shrugged and started Synapse anyway, on a configuration already known to be broken. A missing `SERVER_NAME` or a failed config generation produced a running-but-wrong container instead of a loud stop.

It now stops, with the reason in the log. This affects every guard in the container, not just the new ones.

## Licensing

`LICENSE` has always been AGPL-3.0, but the image label claimed Apache-2.0 and the Docker Hub description claimed MIT. All three now say `AGPL-3.0-only`.

## Also in this release

The arm64 build is no longer taken on trust: the MAS binary is checked for library resolution and executed once per target platform during the multi-arch build, so a broken arm64 binary fails the push instead of reaching a user. CI gained a second boot test covering the delegated-auth path, asserting the three conditions Element actually checks before offering QR login, that MAS migrated its own database, and that its secrets survive a restart. The README gained a troubleshooting entry for the one failure mode that looks healthy from every angle: if `public_baseurl` does not match the address clients actually reach, QR linking fails with a generic error and nothing points at the cause. The banner wordmark and claim were refitted alongside the larger logo.
